sections.title: v1.0
sections.intro: The framework you can build on today.

items.title: Records, enums, typed errors, objects
items.text: Every public type comes from the schema and arrives in each language as that language would write it.

items.title: Stores, signals, computeds, keyed lists
items.text: Reactive state in the core; list changes cross as O(change) patches.

items.title: Ten ports with adapters and fakes
items.text: Http, Kv, SecureStore, Fs, Clock, Rng, Log, Timer, Connectivity and Lifecycle, with platform adapters and deterministic Rust fakes.

items.title: Queries and mutations
items.text: Staleness, dedup, retry, optimistic rollback, an offline queue and persistence.

items.title: Streams and cancellation
items.text: Streams with backpressure; cancelling a call drops its future.

items.title: Snapshot and restore
items.text: Stores snapshot for crash recovery.

items.title: Schema-hash gate
items.text: Checked at load and at build; a mismatched UI and core refuse to talk.

items.title: undra dev
items.text: A live core over a WebSocket, rebuilt on save.

items.title: Teaching diagnostics
items.text: Every macro error says what, why and how to fix it.

items.title: 18 contract scenarios on 3 platforms
items.text: The same wire-level scenarios run against the real core on Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript: 54 of 54 pass.

items.title: Adversarial reviews of every core crate
items.text: Signals, runtime, macros and ffi were each reviewed by someone who did not write them.

sections.title: Since v1.0
sections.intro: Landed in the day after v1.0, each behind an ADR and an adversarial review.

items.title: Frame-coalesced delivery (ADR-031)
items.text: The platform mirrors merge queued change-set entries once per frame, bound their backlog and re-observe on overflow; keyed-list firehoses cost ~10x less per frame on the web. Contract scenario S18 proves a 1,000-transaction burst applies in one drain on all three platforms.

items.title: Harsh-conditions benchmark suite and the live stress screen
items.text: Firehose, event firehose, keyed churn, fan-out, stream backpressure, concurrent completions and a soak, with CI budgets that pass on the GitHub runner; the playground's stress screen shows the same numbers live in your browser.

items.title: Swift error channel (ADR-032)
items.text: Generated Swift never traps: calls throw the method's own error, CancellationError or UndraCallError; commands report through onError.

items.title: A schema loader that survives dead-stripping (ADR-029)
items.text: The loaded host core keeps its schema and JNI exports whatever else touched the target directory.

items.title: The name (ADR-030) and the wire magic (ADR-033)
items.text: Keel became Undra before anything was published; the envelope's magic bytes read UNDR.

sections.title: v1.x
sections.intro: In flight for the v1.x releases.

items.title: Distribution
items.text: brew, npm, a curl installer and cargo-from-git. The release pipeline is built, security-reviewed and proved by a green dry run; the three package channels go live with the v1.0.0 tag.

items.title: Device-measured benchmark rows
items.text: The same benchmarks on an iPhone, an Android phone and Chromium, replacing host proxies.

items.title: Android undra dev remote mode
items.text: The Kotlin runtime gains the WebSocket transport the web and iOS already have.

items.title: Dev-client auto-reconnect
items.text: After a rebuild, a running app reconnects to undra dev on its own instead of needing a reload.

items.title: WeakCtx
items.text: Long-lived tasks stop pinning a runtime that was dropped.

items.title: Macro diagnostic polish
items.text: Better wording for the query-in-impl and split-impl cases.

items.title: Swift Port types public
items.text: Custom ports in Swift without the bindgen fallback.

items.title: Full-JSON undra_schema_json
items.text: So the dlopen-based bindgen keeps doc comments.

sections.title: v1.1 and v1.2
sections.intro: Planned for the releases after v1.0. The order may change with what the benchmarks show.

items.title: crates.io publishing
items.text: Publish the crates under a registry-safe prefix; needs its own ADR for the renames.

items.title: Maven Central for the Kotlin runtime
items.text: Depend on it from Gradle without a local build.

items.title: Windows CLI
items.text: Release binaries and docs for the undra command on Windows.

items.title: undra upgrade
items.text: Move a project to a newer Undra version.

items.title: Migration guides
items.text: From Kotlin Multiplatform and from UniFFI.

items.title: A custom domain
items.text: A home for the site and docs that is ours.

items.title: Desktop targets
items.text: macOS, Windows and Linux over the same C ABI.

items.title: A first-party inspector
items.text: Time-travel over change-sets; the wire makes it natural.

items.title: A sync engine
items.text: A separate package, not part of the core.

items.title: Compose Multiplatform interop
items.text: Use an Undra core under a Compose Multiplatform UI.

notPlanned.title: Not planned
notPlanned.text: Shared UI of any kind, and hosted services. Undra owns everything under the pixels and leaves the screens to SwiftUI, Compose and React.
